name: FITS — Flexible Image Transport System
uses: Astronomical images, spectra, event tables, time-series and multidimensional science cubes.
validation: A proper FITS checker reads 80-character cards in 2880-byte blocks and validates headers, HDUs and data layout. Signature sniffing alone is not FITSverify.

name: FITS tile-compressed image
uses: Tile-compressed FITS image extensions and scientific array products.
validation: Use CFITSIO/FITS tools that understand tiled image compression; .fz alone is not proof of a valid FITS file.

name: High-energy astronomy event list
uses: Time-tagged photon or detector events, often a FITS table with mission-specific columns.
validation: Frequently FITS internally, but the event schema and instrument rules are mission-specific.

name: Astronomy light curve
uses: Brightness, flux or signal measurements over time.
validation: Could be a FITS table or plain text. Inspect the real signature and accompanying documentation.

name: High-energy spectra and response files
uses: Spectral measurements, effective area and instrument response for X-ray/high-energy analysis.
validation: Often FITS products with high-energy astronomy conventions; use mission-compatible science software.

name: VOTable
uses: Interoperable XML table format used by Virtual Observatory services.
validation: Check XML syntax and VOTable schema/version; tables may be inline or encoded in binary sections.

name: Common Data Format (CDF)
uses: Time-dependent scientific variables and metadata in solar-terrestrial physics and space science.
validation: Use CDF-aware libraries/tools to inspect variable records, attributes and file integrity.

name: NetCDF / NetCDF-4
uses: Multidimensional labelled arrays for climate, oceans, atmosphere, weather and satellite science.
validation: Use ncdump/ncvalidator or NetCDF-aware tooling; NetCDF-4 is built on HDF5.

name: HDF4 / HDF5
uses: Hierarchical scientific arrays, image bands, instrument measurements and metadata.
validation: Use HDFView/h5dump or HDF4 tools; HDF4 and HDF5 are distinct formats despite similar extensions.

name: HDF-EOS2 / HDF-EOS5
uses: Earth-observation grids, swaths, point data and geolocation conventions on HDF.
validation: Needs HDF and HDF-EOS-aware software; ordinary HDF validity does not validate geospatial structure.

name: TIFF / GeoTIFF
uses: Raster scenes, elevation, land-cover classification and georeferenced imagery.
validation: Check TIFF structure plus GeoTIFF CRS, tie points, pixel scale, no-data and band metadata.

name: JPEG 2000 image
uses: Satellite image bands and compact raster products, including many Sentinel assets.
validation: Requires a JPEG 2000 decoder; ordinary browser image rendering is not guaranteed.

name: Sentinel SAFE product package
uses: Structured Sentinel product folder/package containing measurement assets, XML metadata, previews and manifest files.
validation: Validate package layout, manifest references and product-specific metadata; .SAFE is usually a directory/package, not one binary file.

name: Earth Observation Processing Framework (EOPF) products
uses: Harmonized data models and storage conventions for selected Earth-observation products.
validation: Validation rules depend on product family and storage layout; check collection/product documentation.

name: Cloud Optimized GeoTIFF (COG)
uses: Tiled, overview-enabled GeoTIFF suited to efficient range requests and cloud analytics.
validation: Check internal TIFF structure, tiling, overview layout and HTTP range behavior with COG validators.

name: GRIB / GRIB2
uses: Gridded meteorological observations and numerical weather prediction fields.
validation: Use ecCodes or GRIB-aware tools to inspect messages, editions, grids and product definitions.

name: Zarr multidimensional arrays
uses: Chunked N-dimensional arrays that can be read efficiently from object storage.
validation: Often a directory/store rather than a single file. Check group/array metadata, chunk keys and supported Zarr version.

name: ESRI Shapefile dataset
uses: Vector geometry plus separate attribute, index, coordinate-system and encoding sidecars.
validation: Treat as a set of related files; check required sidecars, CRS, geometry types and DBF field limits.

name: GeoPackage
uses: SQLite-based geospatial container with vector layers, raster tiles and CRS definitions.
validation: Use SQLite/GDAL/OGR to check spatial tables, required metadata and geometry validity.

name: GeoJSON
uses: JSON features containing geographic points, lines, polygons and collections.
validation: Parse JSON, validate GeoJSON structure, coordinate ordering and geometry rings.

name: KML / KMZ
uses: Geographic annotations, overlays, paths and placemarks; KMZ is a ZIP-based package.
validation: Check KML XML and embedded assets for KMZ; verify coordinate references and links.

name: GDAL Virtual Raster
uses: XML descriptor referencing one or more source raster datasets.
validation: Parse XML and verify all referenced source assets resolve; not a standalone raster payload.

name: STAC catalogue/item metadata
uses: Machine-readable SpatioTemporal Asset Catalogues for discovering geospatial data and its assets.
validation: Check STAC version, required fields, links, assets and extension schemas.

name: NASA PDS3 legacy archive
uses: Legacy planetary data labels and instrument products; labels describe record layout and data meaning.
validation: Validate label/data agreement using PDS tools; attached or detached labels and instrument conventions matter.

name: PDS4 planetary science products
uses: XML product labels based on versioned information models, schemas and product definitions.
validation: Use the official PDS Validate tool on labels, referenced files, checksums and product-specific rules.

name: VICAR image / label products
uses: Image processing and instrument products in some planetary and remote-sensing workflows.
validation: Interpret with VICAR-aware tools and the mission label; .img and .lbl are ambiguous without context.

name: USGS ISIS cube
uses: Planetary image cubes and associated labels, used widely in lunar and planetary processing.
validation: Use ISIS tools to inspect cube labels, dimensions, pixel type and attached metadata.

name: SPICE SPK ephemeris kernel
uses: Spacecraft, planet and satellite trajectories / ephemerides.
validation: Use the NAIF SPICE Toolkit to validate and query binary kernels; this inspector only identifies clues.

name: SPICE CK attitude kernel
uses: Spacecraft attitude, pointing and orientation records.
validation: Use SPICE toolkit and mission-specific frame/clock kernels for meaningful checks.

name: SPICE planetary constants kernels
uses: Planetary orientation, physical constants and body-fixed reference information.
validation: Use SPICE tools; .bpc is a common binary PCK extension and .tpc/.pck often denote text kernels.

name: SPICE text kernels
uses: Frames, instruments, leap seconds, spacecraft clocks and meta-kernel lists.
validation: Text can be inspected locally, but semantic validation requires a compatible SPICE toolkit and dependencies.

name: SPICE digital shape kernel
uses: Digital shape and surface models for small bodies and planetary geometry.
validation: Use SPICE DSK routines; binary integrity and shape semantics are not validated by extension sniffing.

name: SPICE event kernel
uses: Event data represented in SPICE's event-kernel subsystem.
validation: Use SPICE tools compatible with the EK subsystem.

name: CCSDS packets / telemetry / telecommand
uses: Standardized packet, telemetry and telecommand data units transported in spacecraft links.
validation: These are protocol standards, not ordinary file extensions. Use a decoder configured for the mission's packet profile.

name: CCSDS CFDP file-delivery protocol
uses: File delivery over space links, including transfer metadata and retransmission handling.
validation: Validate protocol transactions and mission profile; CFDP is not a single disk-file extension.

name: XFDU digital package description
uses: XML-based package description and exchange of digital information, used in space-data workflows.
validation: Check package manifest, XML schema and every referenced file/checksum.

name: Mission-specific raw payload binary
uses: Unprocessed or encoded payload and instrument records; layout is normally defined by mission documentation.
validation: No universal validator. Require the mission data dictionary, packet layout and byte order.

name: Telemetry / packet files
uses: Packet records, telemetry dumps or instrument housekeeping data under local naming conventions.
validation: Extension is not a standard. Validate the defined packet profile and expected record boundaries.

name: Network packet capture
uses: Network traffic captures useful for ground segment and spacecraft-network diagnostics.
agencies: Ground station and mission IT operations
validation: Check capture magic and link-layer type; use Wireshark/tshark for packet analysis.

name: HRIT / LRIT satellite broadcast
uses: High-/low-rate information transmission used in weather satellite image/data broadcast workflows.
validation: Uses mission/system profiles and transport framing; native source products may separately be NetCDF or imagery.

name: ICARTT atmospheric science exchange
uses: Text-based exchange for aircraft and atmospheric research measurements.
validation: Check header fields, version, units and row/column counts using ICARTT-specific conventions.

name: SPASE space-physics metadata model
uses: Machine-readable descriptions of space and solar-terrestrial physics resources, instruments, observatories and datasets.
validation: Validate against the matching SPASE schema and controlled vocabulary version.

name: STEP / ISO 10303 CAD exchange
uses: Interchange of mechanical CAD parts, surfaces and assemblies.
agencies: Spacecraft and aerospace engineering supply chains
validation: Text syntax and schema do not guarantee clean geometry; full checks need a CAD kernel.

name: IGES CAD exchange
uses: Legacy geometry and drawing interchange for engineering surfaces and models.
validation: Check record sections and geometry with CAD software.

name: 3D mesh / scene assets
uses: Surface meshes, geometry, scene graphs and manufacturing asset packages used in engineering and visualisation.
validation: Basic signatures are insufficient; inspect mesh integrity, normals, materials, units and scene references with a format-aware reader.

name: VTK scientific visualization datasets
uses: Scientific fields, meshes, geometry and simulation outputs.
validation: Legacy VTK and XML VTK variants have different parsers. Check declared arrays, topology and data types.

name: CGNS computational fluid dynamics
uses: CFD grid, flow solution and boundary condition exchange.
validation: Use CGNS libraries and tools to verify tree structure and data arrays.

name: Finite-element and solver datasets
uses: Solver input decks and result databases for stress, vibration, thermal and structural modelling.
validation: Text decks can be inspected; binary solver outputs often need the originating solver or supported reader.

name: MATLAB numerical data and scripts
uses: Scientific matrices, instrument analysis, simulation models and processing scripts.
agencies: Research labs and aerospace analysis teams
validation: MAT files have version-dependent encodings; scripts are code, not scientific data products.

name: Python / Jupyter analysis assets
uses: Processing scripts, notebooks, quality-control workflows and reproducible analysis.
validation: Check syntax and notebook JSON/cell structure; executing notebooks is a separate, security-sensitive action.

name: Parquet / Arrow / Feather
uses: Columnar tables for scalable derived-data analytics and performant data pipelines.
agencies: Modern data platforms and research pipelines
validation: Use Apache Arrow/PyArrow or DuckDB to validate schema, metadata, row groups and readable columns.

name: CSV / TSV / plain text
uses: Observation tables, logs, calibration tables, indexes and exported science measurements.
validation: Check encoding, delimiter, quoting, row widths, headers, units and missing-value conventions.

name: XML / JSON / YAML metadata
uses: Product labels, catalogues, processing manifests, telemetry dictionaries and record streams.
agencies: All modern data services; PDS4 uses XML labels
validation: Syntax checks are only the first layer; a versioned schema is required for standards compliance.

name: Archive / compression containers
uses: Dataset bundles, mission product delivery, compressed observations and package downloads.
validation: List archive members, verify checksums and guard against path traversal, nested bombs and oversized expansion.

name: Chinese lunar & planetary data product standards
uses: China's national standards specify lunar/planetary product format and structure, lunar product hierarchy/nomenclature, and lunar metadata. GB/T 33997 defines product structures and data labels/objects; GB/T 33996 addresses product levels and naming. These are standards, not one universal filename extension.
validation: Check the applicable standard version and mission product label/layout. The file may still use common payload forms such as raster/GeoTIFF, XML labels, tabular data or mission-specific binary; do not assume one extension covers all products.

name: Russian space remote-sensing standard product profile (GOST R 59314-2021)
uses: Russian national standard GOST R 59314-2021 defines general composition and formats for automatically processed space remote-sensing products in visible and near-infrared bands. Listed product components include GeoTIFF or JPEG 2000 rasters, JPEG browse images, XML metadata and quality files, text RPC coefficients, world/projection files, vector boundary data using Shapefile and JSON, and cloud masks using GML/KML.
validation: This is a product profile, not a single file format. Check the standard and data-provider specification; verify raster georeferencing, XML schema, RPC/projection metadata and vector layers together.

name: Point cloud and terrestrial / surface scan data
uses: LiDAR point clouds and 3D surface scans for terrain products, spacecraft/planetary analogues, facilities, and engineering metrology.
validation: Use a LAS/LAZ/E57-aware reader. Check version, point record layout, coordinate reference system, scale/offset, bounds, point count and compression method.

name: SQLite databases and local metadata catalogues
uses: Local indexes, catalogue caches, metadata tables and some GIS containers. A SQLite database may have an arbitrary extension.
validation: Check the SQLite header and open with SQLite tooling; schema, integrity and database meaning require additional checks. GeoPackage is a separate SQLite-based standard.

name: Mission documentation, reports and operational logs
uses: Mission documentation, calibration and instrument handbooks, processing reports, READMEs, operation logs and quality-control logs.
validation: PDF/HTML/Markdown/log syntax checks do not validate the referenced science data. Check digital signatures, checksums, version and provenance where supplied.
